posts.name: Sayan Ghosh

posts.name: Aniruddha Jagdale
posts.cooked:
Thanks @sayan , however I’m not interested in knowing how the evaluation script is evaluating the output because at the time of exam I’d be concerned about the correct output but not how the evaluation script is going to work?

I’m more interested in knowing the difference between your output and my output, then I’ll work my way out. I want to know what it is that is setting the two outputs apart.

Moreover, if it works on local correctly then I don’t know why it’s not accepted in the given environment. posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
@sayan

I know we could adjust the flags in our script and based on how “eval” is invoking the “sed”. But see we cannot keep depending on how the evaluation script is written, we may not have that much time in exam.

Hence, if our sed script file is doing the job correctly, the output should match. That should be the evaluation. also I think the evaluation script is not considering -E option from my experience in the BPT problem, and I kept struggling to know where is my sed script going wrong. It turned out that evaluation script was invoking my sed with different flags.

Pls consider this point of letting us write sed script with our own options given alongwith shebang, it is especially helpful for extended REGEX.

Or at least, write in the question how evaluation is going to invoke our sed script, that way we don’t need to traverse to evaluation.sh just to see that one line.

writing for suitable consideration please.

Thank you,

posts.name: Aniruddha Jagdale
posts.cooked: This is what I meant and talking about. Why should there be any dependency on the way evaluation script is written? As long as our script is doing the job correctly, it should be accepted. And like @22f3002925 mentioned, that should be the true evaluation.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Your ability to read through and understand scripts is part of the course learning outcome. You cannot argue about “I will only work with sed and do not want to know how anything else works” — this attitude wont help you in real world.

The evaluation script creates the script.sh in your folder itself, you can simply cat it to see the flags.

Learning why your script is not outputting anything when called a certain way and how to fix it is very much part of the assignment.

This has also been covered in the course syllabus.

posts.name: Aniruddha Jagdale
posts.cooked:
Well, I’ll not write the script based on how it’s being evaluated behind the scenes, unless explicitly mentioned in the question (which is not the case). Also, I wouldn’t waste time first understanding the evaluation script and then write the script at the time of exam.

Moreover, my job is to follow the question and its instructions, which I did. Question doesn’t say or talk about the fact that “Hey, watch out for evaluation script and then write your script“.

That said, I’ll let you win and close this discussion here.

Kind regards,

Aniruddha

posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked: Yes, I completely agree with you from the learning point of view, I was just saying if the question could mention the command that will invoke our sed script. But no issues, we will look at evaluation script if not provided in the question.

posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
Hi, Aniruddha, being a student I understand your point of view I myself struggled for that question, but see instructors are also right. In essence, see that our script despite correct output was failing evaluation, but this was a practice question and really taught us to look at how our scripts are invoked.

So as a fellow student, I would say let’s take instructor’s viewpoint also in good spirit and keep the communication amenable instead of taking a strong view of any issue. Just a request.

Overall learning in Systems Commands has been good due to sessions of instructors / TAs.

All the best for OPPE !

posts.name: Aniruddha Jagdale
posts.cooked:
Hi @22f3002925 ,

Thank you for your kindness and understanding. I do acknowledge your point of view and tender an apology.

Kind regards,

Aniruddha

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: In the OPPE, we will mention how the script is run. Thanks for pointing that out.
